name: Clockface — The 2080s Reconstruction Scene
description: Clockface devotees are obsessed with the 2080s — specifically the decade of the First Infrastructure Wars, when the corponation system was still new and contested, street networks were genuinely ungoverned, and the first generation of BCIs were clunky, visible, and worn with defiant pride. Members reconstruct the era through salvaged and fabricated first-gen BCI hardware worn externally as jewelry, fashion that references the utilitarian-military crossover of that period, and a music revival built around the raw neural-feedback sound of early BCI-assisted composition. Unlike the Twenty-Twentiers or Nineties Church, Clockface isn't mourning a lost innocence — they're mourning a lost radicalism, a moment when the outcome still felt undecided. The scene's internal status hierarchy is called the Signal Chain, from Static (newcomers) up through Carrier and Broadcast to the rare Amplitude designation for those considered authentic scene pillars.
cultural_impact: Clockface has introduced a new generation to the political history of corponation formation that corporate-controlled education systems have carefully softened, functioning as an accidental history movement that connects aesthetic nostalgia to present-day resistance politics. Several Clockface venues have become informal organizing spaces for Open Architecture and anti-proprietary aug activists.
locations: The Static, a basement venue in a Tier 2 residential block, Milwaukee corridor
Eighty-Eight Steps, an outdoor gathering site on a decommissioned rail bridge, Tier 2-3 border
Carrier Market, a monthly pop-up trading event for 2080s hardware and fashion
story_hooks: A Clockface archivist has located what appears to be genuine 2080s footage of the founding negotiations of a major corponation — footage that contradicts the official corporate history and implicates current executives' predecessors in war crimes — and multiple parties want it suppressed or stolen.

The reproduction first-gen BCI hardware that Clockface members wear as fashion is mostly inert — but a batch circulating at the Carrier Market has turned out to contain active legacy firmware that is picking up and retransmitting fragments of modern BCI communications, accidentally creating a surveillance network.

A Clockface Amplitude-level figure is quietly being paid by a corponation to keep the scene focused on aesthetics and away from genuine political organizing — a younger Static member has discovered the arrangement and must decide what to do with the information.
